note: `sigil` renders TWO DIFFERENT TREES and that is the story worth opening: `true` wraps the input in the prerequisite field's affix layout — a bordered flex box that insets its content and reserves a gap for the `@` cap — and `false` drops the wrapper entirely, because a field with no affix that kept it showed a visible seam at its left edge. The cap itself is conditional on top of that: it appears only while the value is a bare roll-data path, so `1d20 + @abilities.dex.mod` keeps the wrapper and loses the cap.

states.hover: No prop; see the plinth's pseudo-class readout.
states.focus-visible: No prop. It is a real `<input type="text">` and takes the manager's own field focus treatment — border to accent-border, no glow. Tab to it on the plinth.
states.loading: No prop. The expression is a string the caller holds; nothing is resolved asynchronously, and the resolved-value readout `library.html:1510` describes is a player-side surface this component does not draw.
states.invalid: No prop and no mark. `@1d4`, an unclosed parenthesis and a character-data path written without its leading `@` all render identically, because the only writer here is `toStoredRollDataExpression` and it rewrites rather than rejects. Validation belongs to the editor around it, which is where a wrong expression is actually reported.
states.readonly: No prop. `disabled` is the only off state; a `readonly` attribute would have to arrive through `inputAttrs`, which the component's contract restricts to attributes and `data-*` hooks.
states.empty: `value: ""` renders the placeholder, which is a prompt rather than a stated empty state — and with `sigil` on it also renders the `@` cap, because an empty value still matches the bare-path test.

unknobbed.why: The value stamped into `data-roll-data-expression`, so a caller's own tests and the smoke harness can tell one expression field from another on the same screen. It has no visual consequence at all.
